newsitem.title: UK: UK longer leading index at lowest point since 1980.
newsitem.headline: UK longer leading index at lowest point since 1980.

text.p: Britain's longer leading index fell for the seventh month in a row in March and has now hit its lowest level since July 1980, NTC Research said on Friday.

Rising interest rates and a downturn in the gilt yield curve were the principal factors behind the fall in recent months. In March, they were compounded by a fall in contributions from housing starts and the Confederation of British Industry's business optimism index, NTC said.
The longer index read 91.2 in March, down from 91.6 in February.

The shorter leading index was fractionally lower at 99.4 in March as a drop in new car registrations and the EC/GfK consumer confidence index were not quite offset by a rise in share prices and CBI data showing a rise in new orders.
Britain's coincident index fell for the fifth successive month in March as industrial production and CBI stocks of raw materials tailed off.

The lagging index, however, rose to 103.2 in February from 101.8 the month before as further falls in unemployment and a slight pick-up in engineering orders on hand more than outweighed a drop in manufacturing employment.

NTC has picked up the baton of cyclical indicator figures since the Office for National Statistics stopped producing them in February. It uses an indentical methodology to that previously used by the ONS.
The longer leading index signals turning points in the economy some 13 months in advance, the shorter index indicates turning points about five months ahead.
The coincident index moves in line with the business cycle and the lagging index shows turns about a year after they have happened.
